ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
We have three horizontal lines and three parallel, sloped lines. Both of the circles shown touch four of the lines. X, Y and Z are the areas of the grey regions. $\mathrm{D}$ is the area of the parallelogram PQRS. At least how many of the areas $\mathrm{X}, \mathrm{Y}, \mathrm{Z}$ and $\mathrm{D}$ does one have to know in order to be able to determine the area of the parallelogram $\mathrm{T}$ ?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows three horizontal parallel lines and three parallel sloped lines, forming a 2-by-2 set of parallelogram cells inside the outer parallelogram PQRS. The lower-left grey circle is labeled X and touches the lower and middle horizontal lines and the left and middle sloped lines. The upper-right grey circle is labeled Z and touches the middle and upper horizontal lines and the middle and right sloped lines. The lower-right grey parallelogram cell is labeled Y, and the upper-left parallelogram cell is labeled T. Reasoning: Let a be the perpendicular distance between the lower and middle horizontal lines, and let b be the perpendicular distance between the middle and upper horizontal lines. Since circle X touches both those lower/middle horizontal lines and also the left/middle sloped lines, the perpendicular distance between the left and middle sloped lines is also a. Similarly, circle Z implies that the perpendicular distance between the middle and right sloped lines is b. For two fixed families of parallel lines meeting at angle theta, the area of a cell with strip widths u and v is uv/sin(theta). Thus area(Y) = ab/sin(theta), and area(T) = ba/sin(theta). Therefore T = Y. So knowing the single area Y determines T. With zero known areas, the scale is undetermined, so T cannot be determined. Hence the minimum number is 1.

method.method_draft: First read the image as a 3-by-3 line arrangement: three horizontal lines and three parallel sloped lines form four small parallelogram cells inside PQRS. The large grey circle X lies in the lower-left cell and touches its four boundary lines; the small grey circle Z lies in the upper-right cell and touches its four boundary lines. The grey region Y is the lower-right parallelogram cell, and T is the upper-left parallelogram cell. From the text, use that X, Y, Z are areas of grey regions and D is the area of the whole parallelogram PQRS. Let the perpendicular distance between the lower and middle horizontal lines be a, and between the middle and top horizontal lines be b. Because circle X touches the lower/middle horizontals and the left/middle sloped lines, the perpendicular distance between the left and middle sloped lines is also a. Similarly, because circle Z touches the middle/top horizontals and the middle/right sloped lines, the perpendicular distance between the middle and right sloped lines is b. For two families of parallel lines meeting at a fixed angle, the area of any cell equals the product of the two corresponding strip widths divided by sin(theta). Thus area(Y)=a*b/sin(theta) and area(T)=b*a/sin(theta), so T=Y. Therefore knowing the single area Y determines T. Zero known areas cannot determine a nonzero scale-dependent area, so the minimum number is 1.
